\begin{tablenotes}[flushleft]
\footnotesize
\item \textit{Notes:} Each row is a comparison whose statistical significance the text states, on the \rheSzDays{} post-warmup days of $\mathcal T_{\mathrm{opt}}$. $\bar\Delta$ is the mean daily return differential at mid-quotes in percent of the straddle premium (the mean return itself in the last panel), and $\Delta\SR$ the difference of the annualized Sharpe ratios of Section~\ref{sec:rh_econ_measures}. The $t$-statistics test $\bar\Delta = 0$ with the Newey--West long-run variance: at lag truncation $q_{\mathrm{NW}} = \lfloor 4(T/100)^{2/9}\rfloor = \rhrRobLagNW$ \citep{NeweyWest1994} and at $q_{\mathrm{NW}} = \lfloor 1.5\,T^{1/3}\rfloor = \rhrRobLagOld$, both with standard normal $p$-values, and at bandwidth $S = \lceil 1.3\,T^{1/2}\rceil = \rheHACS$ with fixed-$b$ $p$-values \citep{LazarusLewisStockWatson2018,KieferVogelsang2005}, $T = \rheSzDays$. LW is the $p$-value of the \citet{LedoitWolf2008} test of equal Sharpe ratios (circular block bootstrap, block length \rheLWBlock{}, \rheLWBoot{} resamples). The text uses the fixed-$b$ test for statements about mean returns and the LW test for statements about Sharpe ratios. All $p$-values are two-sided.
\end{tablenotes}
